sections.title: Little words that move
sections.content: fel ("up") and hozzá ("to it", the word you met with kell hozzá) both attach naturally to a recipe verb — vág fel is "cut up" and hozzáad is "add [to it]". In the imperative, they naturally split off and follow the command form, instead of staying glued to the front.

items.spanish: Vágd fel, aztán add hozzá a fazékhoz.
items.english: Cut it up, then add it to the pot.

sections.content: add is just ad's ("to give") own imperative — hozzáad literally means "give to it", so add hozzá is the most natural way to say "add it" once you know both pieces separately.
